checked_decisions.finding: Battle-order dialogue (push through, prioritize large types, main-gun/AAM salvo, combat formation, booster breakthrough) matches the source with no reversed objectives or swapped actors.

Eureka's captured-monologue block (dialogue_10639-10648) about her precious people and willingness to stop wishing if it costs the planet is translated in full meaning with no dropped sentence endings; 'those precious to me' / 'everyone' referents kept as the source leaves them, without inventing who else is meant.

月光号 (Gekko) takes damage and 本艦 ("this ship", the speaking ship's self-reference) orders abandonment; translation keeps 'This ship' generic per the source rather than asserting it is explicitly named Gekko in row 10657, matching the translator's own uncertainty note. No meaning fix needed - the source itself does not name the ship in that row.
Unattributed Gekkostate-pilot lines translated with generic subject/addressee, no gender or identity invented, consistent with BASE_RULES.
Garrod/Tiffa and Gainer/Sara exchanges (fighting for the two of them; Gainer always thinking of Sara first) preserve speaker/addressee direction and do not swap who is reassuring whom.

'This fight of mine began with an Antibody Coralian' / 'And that's how we met' reproduces the source's ambiguous handoff between what reads as Renton's masculine-register line and a following collective 'we met' line; no speaker identity is asserted beyond what the source supports, matching the translator's own flagged uncertainty.
Renton's appeal to the Nirvash ('I need Eureka by my side') keeps the emotional escalation and the final need-statement intact, no dropped clauses.
Amita Drive activation through the Command Cluster approach and the crew's parting lines to Renton (bring Eureka back, don't come back empty-handed) match the source's meaning and tone throughout.
